desc: SOURCE causal chain (code-search): use_rcb_time()==false under --no-rcb-time --max-timeslice disabled => guest branch retirement adds ZERO vtime (lib.rs:359-475 doubly gated), no PMU preemption armed (tool_local.rs:2052 + unit test target_only_mode_does_not_create_a_pmu_deadline), step2d gated on empty run_queue with no future timed_waiter (scheduler.rs:1989/2205), committed creeps NANOS_PER_SCHED=500us x500 strict.

EMPIRICAL background signatures in a bare --no-rcb-time boot: 'Skipping global time ahead'=0, SleepUntil(LogicalTime(0)) dominates (384704 vs 115 future), committed races +1425s, rcbs:0 -- YET the boot SUCCEEDS (wedge-off/filecon reach PASS ts1.903). So the signatures are the substrate, not the wedge discriminator.

Single-variable A/B on bare busybox, identical --no-rcb-time config, ONLY var = +2 listening sockets: boot_qemu_off.sh (-serial stdio) BOOTS; boot_qemu_filecon.sh (-serial file:) BOOTS; boot_qemu_sock.sh (-serial file: + serial-unix + QMP) WEDGES frozen at hpet0 ts0.716.

Same-config wedge-vs-green per-dtid diff (237): WEDGE has an extra socket-poller thread (fingerprint clock_gettime x166156, poll x13846, read x13846; 208674 turns=32.3%) ABSENT in GREEN; vCPU/serial-writer gets ~equal ABSOLUTE turns in both (289810 wedge vs 292381 green) -> NOT aggregate turn-starvation; sockets add +45% total turns (646k vs 446k) perturbing interleaving so HPET calibration never completes. H1 scheduler signatures identical in both (non-discriminating).

H7 clock-lag KILL: post-#1190 wedge log (hermit @1ece0654) guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC late reads 1767228032.485..0.553s vs final committed 1767228032.553s -> tracks to ~ms, NOT the pre-#1190 ~8.53s lag (aa5258b: guest ~630.4 vs committed ~639.03). #1190 clock unification holds.

Bisect matrix (results.csv): bare-qemu (no hermit) GREEN control; f6c836b1 (tag demo-20260729 'last-known-green') actually HANGs at qemu-startup 2/2 (300s & 600s); 61d8df39 (#1190) HANGs at hpet; ae2565be HANGs at hpet. Landscape NON-MONOTONE (window-start wedges WORSE than window-end) => no single green anchor inside the window; the ~1min-good is the earlier 2a7ca98.

237 per-dtid starvation query on the parent-controller BAD trace (aa5258b): QEMU dtid9 ran 34 syscalls (last read#34 loading libpixman COMPLETES, runnable) then 94.3% of run (+874s committed) never scheduled again; busy-poller controller dtid7 27,597 syscalls. GOOD (2a7ca98): dtid9 112,506 syscalls, EXITED.
rcb-time ON greens (crawl): committed_time advances with nonzero RCB contribution and crosses the deadline; boot completes ~5x slower than pre-regression sub-minute.

Classification: the wedge is a deterministic livelock (not seed/interleaving-random); rcb-time boot is decision-deterministic -> --no-rcb-time EXPOSES a foundation gap (scheduler-vtime-jump-unproductive-pollers) rather than masking a determinism bug.
Q3 SACRED gate: contrasting-host-load decision traces byte-identical over 41043 turns; only verify-excluded committed_time drifts <=238ns. No wall-clock read in any decision path.

Perf metrics: green rcb-ON ~1,000 timeslices/~200s vtime; 3-knob busybox (boots) ~85k timeslices/~1,450s vtime; wedge 10^5-10^6 timeslices. Crawl is a workaround; sub-minute parity untestable without a scheduler-side fix.

norcb K=100000 90s wall: vtime_burned=393.46s while guest_ts frozen at 0.0797s (owner's ~400x vtime/guest decoupling, live). turns=122411, su0=108687 (88.8% zero-duration polls), su_future=6439 (future timed waiters DO exist), preempt_events=0 (no burn-out fires under --no-rcb-time). vtime_per_turn=3.21ms.

rcbtime healthy in-progress runs (ctrl-valid run-9/10): preempt_events=272-310; preemption BEGINS only at turn ~39294 (long deadline-less warm-up even in rcbtime, explains H2 crawl) and CONTINUES to within 1-3 turns of the tail => NO PMU rearm-failure in booting runs. 0 skids. Need a WEDGED/skid rcbtime run to test H9.

SMOKING-GUN MECHANISM (refined from owner framing). In norcb log the 6439 nonzero SleepUntil targets are NOT stuck far below committed: they track ~74-75ms ahead of current committed and ARE delivered (6439 committed). Consecutive targets step by ~74000000ns=74ms. So the guest is stuck in a ~74ms relative-timeout poll loop (early-boot HPET/timer calibration); Detcore commits each poll-timeout in sequence, inflating committed_time ~74ms/poll (~5300 polls -> 393s vtime) WITHOUT the vCPU thread ever executing the instructions that finish calibration. Future timers DO fire; they are all unproductive epsilon-polls. Correction to 'timer stuck below committed never fired': the decoupling is real (400x) but its form is unproductive-poll-timeout inflation, not a starved-below-committed deadline. rcb-time supplies the missing burn-out: PMU preemption forces vCPU RCB/icount progress between polls. dtid17 busiest (73730 commits) = QEMU main-loop poller.
